prompt: You want to submit a one-line NULL-pointer-check fix to a driver under drivers/staging/ in the Linux kernel. Where should you look FIRST for a concrete, maintainer-endorsed task before writing any code?
choices: The driver's own TODO file inside its drivers/staging/<driver>/ directory
A GitHub 'good first issue' label on the mirror repo
The kernel's CHANGELOG file
Stack Overflow questions tagged 'linux-kernel'

prompt: What does the Signed-off-by line added by `git commit -s` actually certify in a kernel or U-Boot patch?
choices: That the author has the right to submit the code under the project's license (the Developer's Certificate of Origin)
That the patch passed checkpatch.pl with zero warnings
That a maintainer has already reviewed and approved the patch
That continuous integration successfully built the patch

prompt: A patch gets review feedback asking you to fix two more CamelCase fields you missed. What is the correct way to resend it under the mailing-list workflow?
choices: Send a complete v2 patch via git format-patch -v2 with a changelog below the --- line, fixing exactly what was requested
Reply to the thread with just a small diff showing only the two new lines changed
Force-push an amended commit to your fork and reply 'updated'
Open a new, unrelated patch thread so the history stays clean

prompt: In Zephyr's GitHub PR workflow, what effectively replaces the human step of a kernel maintainer manually checking for a missing Signed-off-by line?
choices: A DCO bot that runs automatically and blocks merge until sign-off is present
Nothing -- Zephyr does not require Signed-off-by at all
The Twister test runner, which treats missing sign-off as a build failure
A pre-commit git hook that silently adds sign-off on push

prompt: You run `./scripts/get_maintainer.pl 0001-my-patch.patch` and it prints 'Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (supporter:STAGING SUBSYSTEM)' plus two mailing lists. What should you do with that output?
choices: Send the patch via git send-email with Greg as --to and the listed mailing lists as --cc
Ignore it -- maintainers are auto-subscribed to all patches tagged for their subsystem
Open a GitHub issue tagging Greg Kroah-Hartman
Use it only to decide whether to bother submitting at all, not for addressing the email

prompt: A maintainer's reply says: 'checkpatch --strict on this file still reports: WARNING: Missing a blank line after declarations, #118.' What is the most defensible next action?
choices: Add the missing blank line, re-run checkpatch --strict until it's clean, then resend
Reply explaining that the warning is just a style preference and can be ignored
Resend the patch unchanged since the original logic was already correct
Open a new patch disabling that checkpatch rule for the whole file

prompt: Which of these is a structural consequence of the mailing-list patch model (Linux, U-Boot) that does NOT apply to Zephyr's GitHub PR model?
choices: A revised patch must be resent as a complete, standalone vN patch rather than amended in place on a persistent branch
Patches require a Signed-off-by line
Reviewers can leave comments pointing at a specific change
Continuous integration can run against the submitted code

prompt: Before committing real effort to an open GitHub issue on a project like Zephyr, which check is LEAST useful for judging tractability?
choices: Whether the issue has more than 50 words in its title
Whether a maintainer has confirmed the bug rather than it being an unconfirmed user report
Whether an existing PR already addresses the same file/function
Whether the fix is scoped to one function versus requiring a broader API/locking redesign
